# Meal Manager — full agent guide

This document tells an LLM client (or its operator) how to interact with a Meal Manager instance.

## What Meal Manager is

A self-hosted family app to manage:
- **Inventory** (pantry + fridge), with quantities in canonical units (`g`, `ml`, `unit`).
- **Recipes**, each with an ingredient list, servings, instructions.
- **Weekly menus** (breakfast/lunch/dinner × 7 days).
- **Shopping lists** derived from a menu (menu × servings − current inventory).
- **Ingredients catalog** (the master list referenced by inventory, recipes, shopping).

All data is scoped to a **household**. A user belongs to at most one household at a time, and can share it with other family members.

## Integration: MCP HTTP/SSE

Meal Manager exposes a **Model Context Protocol** server at `POST /mcp` (with `GET /mcp` and `DELETE /mcp` per the StreamableHTTP transport spec). Operates in stateless mode: each POST is self-contained.

### Authentication

Bearer Personal Access Token (PAT) in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer mm_pat_<22 base64url chars>
```

- Tokens are created from `/settings/tokens` in the web UI.
- Each token is **bound to a specific (user, household)** at issuance time and cannot be retargeted.
- The plaintext is shown **once** at creation. Only its SHA-256 hash is persisted. If lost, create a new one.
- Tokens are revocable from the same UI. Revocation takes effect immediately.

On any auth failure, the server responds `401 Unauthorized` with:
```
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="meal-manager-mcp"
```

OAuth 2.1 is on the roadmap — both schemes will coexist when added.

### Tools available (read-only in v1)

All eight tools are read-only. None accept `householdId` as input — it is always derived from the PAT.

| Tool | Purpose | Arguments |
|---|---|---|
| `mealmanager_list_inventory` | List current inventory items (id, ingredient name, category, quantity, location). | `{ location?: "pantry" \| "fridge" }` |
| `mealmanager_list_recipes` | List household recipes (id, title, servings, updatedAt). | `{ query?: string }` (title substring) |
| `mealmanager_get_recipe` | Full recipe details with ingredient list. | `{ recipeId: string }` (UUID) |
| `mealmanager_get_menu_for_week` | Menu for a given week. Creates an empty menu if none exists (idempotent — matches the web behavior). | `{ weekStart: string }` (ISO date `YYYY-MM-DD` of a Monday) |
| `mealmanager_get_shopping_list` | Shopping list snapshot for a menu. | `{ menuId: string }` (UUID) |
| `mealmanager_list_ingredients` | Ingredients catalog (master list). | `{ query?: string, category?: string, storage?: "pantry"\|"fridge", includeArchived?: boolean }` |
| `mealmanager_get_ingredient` | Full ingredient details with products attached. | `{ ingredientId: string }` (UUID) |
| `mealmanager_get_household` | Current household (id, name, members). | `{}` |

Each tool returns a single `text` content block containing the JSON-pretty-printed result of the underlying use case.

### Units

All quantities are stored in canonical units:
- Mass → `g` (grams)
- Volume → `ml` (millilitres)
- Discrete → `unit`

Conversions (kg ↔ g, L ↔ ml, cl ↔ ml, mg ↔ g) happen at the API boundary, not inside tool responses. The agent receives values in the canonical unit and can convert for display.

## Example: Claude Desktop config

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "meal-manager": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://your-domain.example/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer mm_pat_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Example: Home Assistant (for voice via Google Nest / Gemini)

Today (May 2026) a Google Nest device cannot natively call third-party MCP servers. The pragmatic path for voice control is:

1. Install **Home Assistant** with the MCP client integration.
2. Add Meal Manager as an MCP server in HA (same URL + Bearer PAT as above).
3. Expose the resulting HA entities to Google Assistant via the official HA → Google Assistant integration.
4. "Hey Google, ask Home Assistant what's in the fridge" → HA proxies to Meal Manager via MCP.

Alternative: write a custom Gemini API client that uses MCP as a tool source.

## Architecture notes (for LLMs that read code)

- Hexagonal per bounded context under `server/contexts/<context>/{domain,application,infrastructure}`.
- The MCP transport layer is at `server/routes/mcp/`.
- The PAT domain lives in `server/contexts/platform/` alongside `User`.
- Hexagonal boundary rule: `domain` MUST NOT import frameworks. ESLint enforces this.

## Spec source

Read-only spec snapshots live under `openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md`. The MCP integration was introduced by change `add-mcp-llm-integration`. Look at `openspec/changes/archive/` for archived proposals once shipped.
